key_insight: The paper develops an ALE finite-volume solver for relativistic detonation waves and shows that relativistic pressure-jump behavior differs qualitatively from Newtonian detonations, including a nonmonotonic Zel'dovich pressure jump.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical numerical tool for simulating high-speed reactive relativistic flows in astrophysics and other extreme-energy systems where shock tracking and stiff reactions are difficult.
method: Second-order ALE finite-volume scheme with TVD reconstruction
Mesh velocity set equal to the shock speed to follow the front accurately
Locally implicit treatment of stiff reaction source terms plus an efficient conserved-to-primitive recovery algorithm
evidence_signal: The solver successfully reproduces the Zel'dovich-von Neumann-Doering detonation profile up to shock Lorentz factors of about 7.
watch_item: The approach relies on accurate shock-speed tracking and robust primitive-variable recovery, which may become challenging for stronger shocks or more complex reaction models.
paper_title: An Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian solver for relativistic detonation waves
